Choose it when both spatial resolution and temporal consistency must be improved simultaneously [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method should be chosen when 'both spatial resolution and temporal consistency must be improved simultaneously.' However, the evidence in Source [S1] describes two distinct approaches for joint spatial and temporal super-resolution: STNet and STSRNet. The physics-informed method by Werhahn et al. (which matches the 'unofficial' note details like multi-pass GAN and orthogonal slice passes) is described as performing volumetric spatial upscaling (8x per dimension) on smoke simulations. The text does not state that this specific physics-informed method improves temporal consistency or performs joint spatiotemporal upscaling; rather, it focuses on spatial resolution and physical consistency via governing equations. The methods explicitly noted for joint spatial and temporal dimensions are STNet and STSRNet, not the Werhahn et al. method described in the notes. Therefore, the evidence does not support the claim that this specific physics-informed method is the choice for simultaneous spatial and temporal improvement.
